items.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021
items.q: back like John Philip Sousa or something back in the day

ctx.x: Did the Easley family create a reputation in Olean and the surrounding area as those music people? Call them when you need music?

Well actually my mother, that was the Barnes family, you see. Barnes. And say for instance my mother’s mother, my grandmother is the one that went to conservatory in Meadville, Pennsylvania. But her father was a band master. In other words he played all the instruments — back like John Philip Sousa or something back in the day, and he played all of the instruments and his son, which would have been my great uncle Darwin played saxophone and my mother’s brother Darwin played saxophone. So I’m a fourth generation…
If I could go back in time and drop in on a gig that you were on when you were about fifteen with the family band and write down every tune that you played, what would some of those titles be?
